phase_statuses.title: Extend reporting domain model and strict resource mapping
phase_statuses.objective: Extend `work_reports` to persist the real workbook reporting fields and add a strict resource mapping table that resolves workbook resource information into workshop, line, and process scope.
dependencies: existing line topology and capacity compare logic
deliverables: backend tests for persistence and mapping behavior
phase_statuses.evidence_expectation: schema inspection or migration-backed assertions, backend unit tests for persistence and mapping, and code references showing query and compare compatibility

acceptance_criteria.text: `work_reports` persists the required workbook business fields, including operator code and name, section leader name, dispatch number, product code, product name, product specification, resource group name, resource name, department name, and source workbook metadata, without breaking report queries.

A strict resource mapping table resolves `resource_group_name + resource_name + source_process_code` to exactly one `company_code + workshop_code + line_code + process_code`, and missing or ambiguous mappings produce explicit errors.
Reporting query responses expose the new persisted fields so the frontend no longer depends on placeholder filler or section-leader values.
Existing same-day capacity compare selection continues to rely on stored `report_local_date + workshop_code + line_code + process_code` values without fallback behavior.

phase_statuses.title: Build xlsx preview and commit import pipeline
phase_statuses.objective: Add fail-fast `.xlsx` preview and commit APIs that parse multiple workbook sheets, validate each row with explicit failure reasons, and persist only rows that pass strict validation.
deliverables: explicit error handling for missing order or mapping and ambiguous mapping
backend tests for preview and commit
phase_statuses.evidence_expectation: backend API or service tests for preview and commit, assertions on row-level validation payloads, and query assertions proving persisted source metadata and mapped keys

acceptance_criteria.text: The backend preview flow parses the provided `.xlsx` workbook format across multiple sheets and preserves sheet name plus source row number in preview results.
Preview returns row-level validation results with explicit reasons for missing order, missing mapping, ambiguous mapping, invalid required fields, or other strict validation failures.
Commit persists only rows that passed preview validation and writes the mapped reporting fields plus workbook provenance into `work_reports`.
Commit does not invent default workshop, line, process, or master-data values when required data is missing; it fails explicitly instead.

phase_statuses.title: Upgrade frontend import and reporting UI to real workbook fields
phase_statuses.objective: Replace the current text import flow with `.xlsx` preview/commit UX and update the reporting records table to display the real workbook fields while preserving the same-day capacity compare experience.
deliverables: browser tests for success and failure paths
regression coverage for `当日产能` compare on imported rows
phase_statuses.evidence_expectation: frontend build output, Playwright evidence for preview and commit, and browser assertions showing imported rows still participate in capacity compare

acceptance_criteria.text: The frontend import flow accepts `.xlsx`, shows a preview before commit, and surfaces backend row-level validation results clearly to the user.
The reporting records table displays real report fields such as order number, dispatch number, product code, process code and name, resource, operator, section leader, quantity, and `当日产能`.
After importing rows with valid mappings, blank compare cells on imported reports still open the existing compare modal and keep the same strict same-day compare rules.
Browser validation covers one successful workbook import path and one explicit failure path from the real UI.
